newsitem.title: UK: Irish INLA guerrillas say they shot policeman.
newsitem.headline: Irish INLA guerrillas say they shot policeman.

text.p: A small band of outlawed Irish Catholic guerrillas said on Saturday that they had killed an off-duty Northern Ireland policeman shot in a crowded Belfast bar on Friday night.
The Irish National Liberation Army (INLA), a republican extremist group which has killed a number of British security forces personnel in the past, made the claim in a telephone call to the BBC.
A caller using a recognised codeword rang the BBC in Belfast and said he was speaking on behalf of the INLA.
"We executed the policeman last night in the Parliament Bar," he said. The INLA was formed 1975 and has been responsible for many killings in the 30-year Northern Ireland conflict.

The Irish Republican Army -- which has carried out a number of attacks in Northern Ireland and on the British mainland since its ended a 17-month ceasefire in February 1996 -- earlier denied involvement in the killing.
Police officer Darren Bradshaw was singled out by a gunman who shot him as he sat drinking in the Parliament Bar near the centre of Belfast late on Friday.
